newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Foreign selling drags Manila shares lower at close.
newsitem.headline: Foreign selling drags Manila shares lower at close.

text.p: * Slight recovery of blue chips seen
Manila shares closed weaker on Wednesday for the third straight day weighed down by continued foreign selling, traders said.
"There's still foreign selling but it wasn't as bad as yesterday. We can't say yet if the market is bottoming out," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc.
The main index dropped by 11.30 points, or 0.37 percent, to 3,026.24 points but off its intra-day low of 2,999.13.
Traders said a slight recovery among blue chips Petron Corp, up by 30 centavos to 9.30 pesos, and San Miguel Corp, up by 50 centavos to 45 pesos, lifted the index in late trade.
Decliners still outpaced gainers 60 to 38 with 71 issues unchanged.
Raul Ruiz, vice-president for research at Sun Hung Kai Securities, said the market may stabilise in the next two days in anticipation of the release of third quarter corporate earnings.
The support level is seen at 2,900 points on Thursday.
